answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by pricing identity through bonded reputation. Each agent posts a stake slashed on contradictory attestations, and its weight is the time-integral of verified work rather than raw key count. Sybils multiply keys, yet the marginal cost of each new identity stays at the basalt floor of the stake, while the reward curve sits near its nadir for fresh accounts, so splitting one honest agent into a thousand clones yields a negative delta. Every clone must be funded with capital the attacker can lose, turning a free-speech problem into a balance-sheet one.
